questions.question:
GuardDuty reports that an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group is communicating with a known command-and-control server. The security team must contain the instance while preserving it for forensic analysis.

Which combination of actions should the security engineer take FIRST?

options.text: Enable termination protection, detach the instance from the Auto Scaling group and its load balancer target group, and replace its security groups with an isolation security group.
Terminate the instance and let the Auto Scaling group launch a clean replacement.
Stop the instance immediately and create an AMI of it for later analysis.
Reboot the instance to end the malicious process, then rotate the instance profile role.

questions.explanation: Contener sin destruir evidencia: protección contra terminación, sacarla del ASG (para que no la termine o reemplace) y del balanceador, y aislarla en red. Detener o reiniciar pierde la memoria volátil, y terminar destruye la evidencia.

questions.question:
A security engineer replaces the security groups of a compromised instance with a security group that has no inbound or outbound rules. The engineer observes that an existing outbound SSH session from the instance is still active.

What is the reason, and what should the engineer do?

options.text: SSH traffic is not filtered by security groups; use AWS WAF to block it.
Outbound rules are evaluated only for new instances; stop and start the instance.
Security group changes take up to 24 hours to propagate; wait and monitor.
Security groups do not interrupt existing tracked connections; add deny rules to the subnet's network ACL to block the traffic immediately.

questions.explanation: Los security groups son stateful: las conexiones rastreadas existentes continúan tras quitar las reglas. Las NACLs son stateless y bloquean el tráfico de inmediato (afectan a toda la subred, así que conviene aislar con cuidado).

questions.question:
Before shutting down a compromised Linux instance, the incident response plan requires preserving evidence of running processes, network connections, and in-memory malware.

What should the security engineer do FIRST?

options.text: Export the VPC Flow Logs of the instance to S3.
Stop the instance so that its state cannot change.
Create EBS snapshots of all attached volumes.
Capture a memory dump of the instance (for example, with a forensic tool through Systems Manager Run Command) and store it in the forensic account.

questions.explanation: El orden de volatilidad indica capturar primero la memoria, que se pierde al detener la instancia; luego los snapshots de disco.

questions.question:
A security engineer must share EBS snapshots of a compromised instance with a dedicated forensic account. The volumes are encrypted with the default AWS managed key aws/ebs.

What should the engineer do?

options.text: Copy the snapshots and re-encrypt them with a customer managed KMS key whose key policy allows the forensic account, then share the copies.
Make the snapshots public for a short time so that the forensic account can copy them.
Disable encryption on the snapshots and share them.
Share the snapshots directly and grant the forensic account access to the aws/ebs key.

questions.explanation: Los snapshots cifrados con una AWS managed key no se pueden compartir porque su key policy no se puede modificar. Se copian con una customer managed key compartida. Hacerlos públicos expone la evidencia.

questions.question:
Forensic evidence collected during incidents must be stored so that nobody, including administrators of the forensic account, can delete or modify it for 7 years.

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Store the evidence in an S3 bucket with Versioning and MFA Delete enabled.
Store the evidence in an S3 bucket with Object Lock in governance mode.
Store the evidence in an S3 bucket in the forensic account with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode and a 7-year retention period.
Store the evidence in EBS volumes with deletion protection enabled.

questions.explanation: El modo compliance impide que cualquier usuario, incluido root, borre o acorte la retención. El modo governance permite eludirla con s3:BypassGovernanceRetention.

questions.question:
A company receives several GuardDuty EC2 findings each week. The security team wants an automated workflow that isolates the instance, acquires memory and disk evidence, and stores it in a forensic account, with minimal custom development.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the Automated Forensics Orchestrator for Amazon EC2 solution, which uses Security Hub findings and AWS Step Functions to orchestrate isolation and evidence acquisition.
Use Amazon Detective to automatically isolate instances in a finding group.
Create an AWS Config rule that stops instances with GuardDuty findings.
Enable GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 and delete infected volumes.

questions.explanation: La solución de AWS orquesta aislamiento, captura de memoria y disco y almacenamiento de evidencia. Detective investiga pero no actúa, y Config no es un mecanismo de respuesta forense.

questions.question:
A developer accidentally committed an IAM user's access key to a public Git repository. The key has administrator permissions.

What should the security engineer do FIRST?

options.text: Rotate the user's console password and enable MFA.
Remove the commit from the Git repository history.
Deactivate the access key, then review CloudTrail for actions performed with the key ID.
Delete the IAM user and all of its resources.

questions.explanation: La prioridad es invalidar la credencial expuesta. Desactivar (en vez de borrar) conserva el key ID para la investigación. Después se busca en CloudTrail lo que hizo el actor (usuarios, roles, claves o recursos creados) y se corrige el origen.

questions.question:
During an investigation, the team finds that an attacker used stolen credentials to create a new IAM user with access keys and several new IAM roles in a compromised account.

What should the security engineer do to ensure complete eradication?

options.text: Identify all resources and identities that the attacker created or modified from CloudTrail and remove them, in addition to invalidating the original credentials.
Invalidate only the original credentials, because the new identities depend on them.
Apply an SCP that denies iam:CreateUser in the account.
Enable GuardDuty in the account, which removes malicious identities automatically.

questions.explanation: Los atacantes crean persistencia (usuarios, roles, claves, funciones). Las identidades nuevas no dependen de las credenciales originales, así que hay que eliminarlas explícitamente.

questions.question:
A GuardDuty finding reports that an IAM role made API calls from an unusual geolocation. The security engineer must quickly determine whether the activity is legitimate.

Which approach provides the MOST context with the LEAST effort?

options.text: Create an AWS Config rule to track changes to the role.
Download the CloudTrail logs from S3 and search them manually with grep.
Enable VPC Flow Logs and wait for new traffic from the role.
Pivot to Amazon Detective from the finding to review the role's activity, geolocations, and API volume compared to its baseline.

questions.explanation: Detective construye un behavior graph con CloudTrail, Flow Logs y hallazgos, y muestra la actividad comparada con la línea base, lo que facilita validar falsos positivos.

questions.question:
A security engineer tries to enable Amazon Detective in an account where GuardDuty was enabled one hour earlier. The operation fails.

What is the reason?

options.text: Detective requires CloudTrail data events for S3.
Detective can be enabled only in the organization's management account.
Detective requires AWS Security Hub to be enabled first.
GuardDuty must have been enabled for at least 48 hours before Detective can be enabled in the account.

questions.explanation: Detective requiere que GuardDuty lleve al menos 48 horas activo en la cuenta antes de habilitarlo.

questions.question:
An analyst sees several GuardDuty findings involving the same EC2 instance, an IAM role, and external IP addresses within a two-hour window. The analyst wants to investigate them as one security event.

Which Detective feature should the analyst use?

options.text: Detective investigations for IAM users, which analyze only one user.
GuardDuty suppression rules.
Finding groups, which group related findings and entities into a single activity.
Security Hub insights.

questions.explanation: Los finding groups relacionan hallazgos y entidades que forman parte de la misma actividad sospechosa, facilitando ver el alcance y la causa raíz.

questions.question:
The security team must determine every action taken in all accounts during the past 18 months by a specific access key. Logs are stored in the organization trail bucket.

Which solution is the MOST cost-effective?

options.text: Use Amazon Athena with a CloudTrail table that uses partition projection, and filter by useridentity.accesskeyid and date.
Load all logs into an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster sized for 18 months of data.
Use Amazon Detective, which retains data for up to 5 years.
Use CloudTrail event history in each account.

questions.explanation: Athena se paga por datos escaneados y consulta los logs en S3 sin infraestructura. El event history solo cubre 90 días, y Detective conserva como máximo 1 año.

questions.question:
A Security Hub finding states that an S3 bucket is public. The owner says that the bucket is intentionally public to host images for a website.

What should the security engineer do to validate and handle the finding?

options.text: Verify that the bucket contains only public website assets (for example, with Macie) and that the access is limited to s3:GetObject, then suppress the finding with a documented justification.
Disable the control in all accounts to avoid future findings.
Delete the finding from Security Hub, because the owner confirmed the access.
Immediately enable Block Public Access on the bucket regardless of the owner's response.

questions.explanation: Validar un hallazgo implica confirmar el contexto, no solo aceptar la explicación. Si es esperado, se suprime con justificación. (La alternativa recomendada suele ser CloudFront con OAC en lugar de un bucket público.)

questions.question:
A company wants incident responders to be able to access any account in the organization within minutes during an incident, with all access logged and without using shared long-term credentials.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Pre-provision an incident response role in every account (for example, with CloudFormation StackSets) that can be assumed only from the security account, and monitor its use with alerts.
Create IAM users with administrator permissions in each account and store the passwords in a vault.
Create the necessary roles during the incident with the management account.
Give responders the root user credentials of each account.

questions.explanation: La preparación incluye roles de respuesta ya desplegados, probados y monitoreados. Crearlos durante el incidente retrasa la respuesta, y las credenciales compartidas impiden la trazabilidad.

questions.question:
A company's DDoS response plan requires help from AWS experts during attacks against its CloudFront distributions and Application Load Balancers, and protection against unexpected scaling charges caused by the attack.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced, protect the resources, and grant the Shield Response Team access with an IAM role.
Use AWS Firewall Manager to deploy security groups to the load balancers.
Rely on AWS Shield Standard and enable AWS WAF rate-based rules.
Open an AWS Support case during the attack to request the AWS DDoS Response Team.

questions.explanation: Shield Advanced incluye acceso al Shield Response Team (requiere plan Business o Enterprise Support), cost protection y detección mejorada. Shield Standard no incluye estos beneficios.

questions.question:
A company with Shield Advanced wants the Shield Response Team to contact the operations team proactively when a DDoS event affects the availability of a protected application.

What must the company configure?

options.text: A Shield Advanced rate-based rule with a Count action.
An SNS topic subscribed by the Shield Response Team.
An AWS Health event rule that forwards events to the team.
Proactive engagement, with Route 53 health checks associated with the protected resources and emergency contacts.

questions.explanation: El proactive engagement requiere health checks de Route 53 asociados a los recursos protegidos para que el SRT detecte el impacto y contacte a los contactos de emergencia.

questions.question:
A security team wants the response to a common finding type (for example, an exposed security group port) to be consistent, repeatable, and auditable, with the ability to run it manually or automatically.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Write the steps in a wiki page that analysts follow during incidents.
Use a CloudWatch dashboard that shows the findings.
Create an AWS Config rule that sends an email for each finding.
Document the playbook and implement it as an SSM Automation runbook that can be invoked from EventBridge or manually, with execution history.

questions.explanation: Los runbooks de SSM Automation codifican pasos, controlan permisos con un rol y registran cada ejecución, lo que permite invocarlos manual o automáticamente.

questions.question:
An automated runbook isolates instances when GuardDuty detects cryptocurrency mining. For production instances, the security team requires that a human approve the isolation step before it runs.

How should the security engineer implement this?

options.text: Send the finding to an SNS topic and isolate the instance if no one responds.
Use a Config rule with manual remediation for production instances.
Add an aws:approve step to the SSM Automation runbook before the isolation step for production instances.
Add an aws:sleep step that waits 30 minutes before isolating the instance.

questions.explanation: aws:approve pausa la ejecución hasta que los aprobadores designados la aprueben o rechacen; puede notificar por SNS.

questions.question:
The security team wants security groups that allow 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22 to be fixed automatically within minutes of creation, across all accounts.

Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an SCP that denies ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress in all accounts.
Use an AWS Config managed rule (restricted-ssh) deployed through an organization conformance pack with automatic remediation using an SSM Automation runbook.
Run a Lambda function every 24 hours that scans all security groups.
Use GuardDuty to detect and delete the rules.

questions.explanation: Config evalúa por cambio de configuración y remedia con SSM Automation en todas las cuentas mediante conformance packs. Denegar la API por completo bloquearía la operación normal.

questions.question:
A company must fail over a critical application to a standby Region during an incident, using a highly reliable mechanism that does not depend on the control plane of the impaired Region.

Which service should the company use?

options.text: AWS Fault Injection Service experiments.
Route 53 latency-based routing with health checks only.
AWS Resilience Hub assessments.
Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller routing controls.

questions.explanation: Route 53 ARC ofrece routing controls con alta disponibilidad para conmutar el tráfico de forma controlada entre Regiones. Resilience Hub y FIS evalúan y prueban, pero no conmutan.

questions.question:
A company wants to run an experiment that stops 30% of the instances behind an Application Load Balancer to verify that alarms trigger and that the incident runbook restores the service. The experiment must stop automatically if customer impact exceeds a threshold.

What should the security engineer configure?

options.text: A Config rule that stops instances when an alarm is triggered.
An AWS FIS experiment template with the stop instances action, a target selection of 30%, and a CloudWatch alarm as a stop condition.
An SSM Automation runbook that stops instances with an aws:approve step.
A Resilience Hub assessment of the application.

questions.explanation: Las plantillas de FIS definen acciones, objetivos (con porcentaje) y stop conditions basadas en alarmas de CloudWatch, que detienen el experimento si el impacto es excesivo.

questions.question:
A team wants to know whether its application can meet a recovery time objective (RTO) of 1 hour and a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes, and receive recommendations to improve resilience.

Which service should the team use?

options.text: AWS Backup audit manager.
AWS Resilience Hub with a resiliency policy that defines the RTO and RPO targets.
AWS Trusted Advisor fault tolerance checks only.
AWS FIS with a stop condition of 1 hour.

questions.explanation: Resilience Hub evalúa la aplicación frente a la política de RTO/RPO y recomienda mejoras, alarmas, SOPs y experimentos de FIS.

questions.question:
The security team discovers that during the last incident, CloudTrail logs in the compromised account had been deleted by the attacker.

Which design change BEST prevents this in the future?

options.text: Increase the CloudTrail event history retention in the account.
Enable CloudTrail Insights in the account.
Enable MFA for all IAM users in the compromised account.
Deliver logs through an organization trail to an S3 bucket in a separate log archive account with Object Lock and restricted access.

questions.explanation: Separar los logs en otra cuenta, con inmutabilidad, evita que un atacante con control de la cuenta comprometida los elimine.

questions.question:
Ransomware encrypted data on EC2 instances in a production account. Backups are in AWS Backup vaults in the same account, and the attacker also deleted recovery points.

Which design change will protect backups in the future?

options.text: Increase the backup frequency in the production account.
Copy backups to a vault in a separate account and enable AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode.
Use EBS snapshots instead of AWS Backup.
Encrypt the backups with the AWS managed key.

questions.explanation: Las copias en otra cuenta con Vault Lock (compliance) no pueden borrarse ni siquiera con privilegios de administrador en la cuenta de producción.

questions.question:
A company subscribes to AWS Security Incident Response. The security team wants AWS to help triage GuardDuty and Security Hub findings and to engage the AWS Customer Incident Response Team (CIRT) during active incidents.

Which capabilities does this service provide?

options.text: Automatic remediation of all findings without customer approval.
Replacement of GuardDuty and Security Hub with a single detection service.
Automated triage of findings, case management, and access to the AWS CIRT around the clock.
Automatic Shield Advanced protection for all resources.

questions.explanation: AWS Security Incident Response tría hallazgos, gestiona casos y da acceso 24/7 al CIRT de AWS; complementa GuardDuty y Security Hub.

questions.question: An IAM role used by a Lambda function was compromised. The function must keep working. Which actions should the security engineer take? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Identify how the credentials were exposed and fix the root cause
Delete the role and the Lambda function
Review CloudTrail for actions performed with the role's sessions
Disable CloudTrail to reduce log noise
Rotate the access keys of the role
Revoke active sessions for the role

questions.explanation: La revocación de sesiones invalida credenciales emitidas antes de ese momento, y Lambda obtiene credenciales nuevas. Los roles no tienen access keys, y borrar el rol rompe el servicio.

questions.question: Which actions preserve the integrity of forensic evidence collected from AWS? (Select THREE.)

options.text: Analyze the original volume in place on the compromised instance
Store evidence in the compromised account
Store evidence in a dedicated forensic account with restricted access
Calculate and record hashes of the evidence files
Share evidence with a public link for quick review
Maintain a chain of custody record for each artifact

questions.explanation: La integridad de la evidencia requiere hashes, almacenamiento aislado y cadena de custodia; se analizan copias, no el original en la instancia comprometida.

questions.question: Order the steps to handle a compromised EC2 instance while preserving evidence.

options.text: Enable termination protection and detach the instance from the Auto Scaling group
Isolate the instance with a restrictive security group and network ACL
Capture the instance memory
Create snapshots of the EBS volumes
Analyze copies of the evidence in the forensic account

questions.explanation: Primero se evita que la instancia desaparezca, luego se aísla, se captura la evidencia volátil (memoria) y después la persistente (discos), y se analizan copias en una cuenta aislada.

questions.question: Order the phases of the incident response lifecycle.

options.text: Preparation
Detection and analysis
Containment, eradication, and recovery
Post-incident activity

questions.explanation: Es el ciclo basado en NIST que sigue la guía de AWS; las lecciones aprendidas vuelven a alimentar la preparación.

questions.question: Match each incident with the MOST appropriate first containment action.

prompts.text: Stolen temporary credentials of a role
Malicious IP attacking a web application

options.text: Block the IP with an AWS WAF IP set
Deactivate the access key
Revoke active sessions of the role
Enable Amazon Macie
Enable S3 Block Public Access
Isolate it with a restrictive security group

questions.explanation: Cada tipo de incidente tiene su contención propia; Macie descubre datos sensibles pero no contiene un incidente.

questions.question: Match each investigation need with the service that BEST meets it.

prompts.text: Visualize entity behavior and baselines for a finding
SQL queries over years of CloudTrail without managing tables
Ad hoc queries on logs stored in S3, paid per query
Inspect packet payloads from an instance

options.text: VPC Traffic Mirroring
Amazon Detective
AWS CloudTrail Lake
AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon Athena

questions.explanation: Cada herramienta aporta una vista distinta de la investigación; Trusted Advisor da recomendaciones, no análisis forense.

questions.question:
Route 53 Resolver query logs show that a compromised instance resolves a domain that is used for data exfiltration. The security team must block resolution of this domain for all VPCs in the organization.

Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Add an AWS WAF rule that blocks the domain on the Application Load Balancers.
Add a deny rule for the domain to each security group.
Create a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule group with a block rule for the domain and deploy it to all VPCs with AWS Firewall Manager.
Create a private hosted zone with the domain in each VPC.

questions.explanation: DNS Firewall filtra consultas salientes por dominio; Firewall Manager lo despliega en toda la organización. Los security groups no filtran por dominio, y WAF protege tráfico entrante.

questions.question:
A company wants forensic analysis tools to be available immediately during incidents without exposing them to the compromised environment.

Which design follows AWS best practices?

options.text: Install forensic tools on every production instance in advance.
Maintain a dedicated forensic account with a pre-built, hardened forensic AMI and isolated VPC, where evidence copies are analyzed.
Download forensic tools from the internet onto the compromised instance during the incident.
Analyze evidence in the log archive account.

questions.explanation: Una cuenta forense aislada con herramientas preparadas evita contaminar la evidencia y alertar al atacante. La cuenta de log archive debe mantenerse solo para almacenar logs.
